title: Netflix's 'Operation Safed Sagar' Brings the IAF's Untold Kargil War Story to Global Audiences
excerpt: Premiering August 7, the series dramatises the Indian Air Force's high-altitude mission during the 1999 Kargil War, featuring Siddharth, Jimmy Shergill, and Dia Mirza in what Netflix calls its first-of-its-kind Indian military drama.
body:
• Netflix's 'Operation Safed Sagar' premieres August 7, telling the story of the Indian Air Force's Golden Arrows Squadron during the 1999 Kargil War
  • The series stars Siddharth, Jimmy Shergill, Abhay Verma, and Dia Mirza, directed by Oni Sen of 'Asur' fame
  • Air Chief Marshal (Retd.) B.S. Dhanoa, who led the real operation, served as a consultant and called it "long overdue"
  • Netflix describes it as India's first war drama series focused on the air force, blending large-scale action with personal stories of pilots and their families

When the Indian Air Force launched Operation Safed Sagar during the 1999 Kargil War, it marked the world's highest-altitude air combat operation. Twenty-seven years later, Netflix is bringing that chapter to screens worldwide with a military drama series that premieres on August 7.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=vqV3xfeb4SQ

Directed by Oni Sen, best known for the thriller series Asur, Operation Safed Sagar follows the Golden Arrows Squadron — one of the IAF's youngest units — as they carried out bombing runs across mountain peaks exceeding 16,000 feet using ageing MiG-21 and Mirage 2000 aircraft against entrenched Pakistani positions.

A Cast Mixing Veterans and Fresh Faces

The ensemble features Siddharth, who returns to Hindi-language projects after years focused on Tamil and Telugu cinema, alongside Jimmy Shergill as a senior officer. Abhay Verma, who broke out in last year's horror hit Munjya, plays one of the young pilots. Dia Mirza, Prajakta Koli, and Adil Hussain round out the principal cast, with Mihir Ahuja, Taaruk Raina, Arnav Bhasin, and Amrita Bagchi in supporting roles.

https://x.com/NetflixIndia/status/2084534805559922853

The series is created by Abhijeet Singh Parmar and Kushal Srivastava, and produced by Sanjay Routray and Sarita Patil of Matchbox Shots LLP along with Mehboob Pal Singh Brar of Feel Good Films.

"India is ready to hear this story now. In fact, it is long overdue. If this series succeeds in igniting that spark and encourages more young Indians to join the Indian Air Force, I would consider that my objective achieved."

— Air Chief Marshal (Retd.) B.S. Dhanoa

The Real Operation

In the summer of 1999, as Pakistani forces occupied strategic positions across the Line of Control in the Kargil sector, the Indian Army called on the air force for support. What followed was a 47-day aerial campaign at altitudes where jet engines lose thrust and pilots face extreme physiological strain. The IAF deployed MiG-21s, MiG-27s, MiG-29s, and Mirage 2000s for precision strikes, losing two aircraft and a helicopter in the process.

Air Chief Marshal (Retd.) B.S. Dhanoa, who flew combat missions during the actual operation and later became IAF chief, served as a consultant on the series. His involvement lends the project an authenticity that previous Kargil-themed films have often lacked.

Why the IAF's Story Has Taken So Long

While Bollywood has told multiple versions of the Kargil ground campaign — from LOC Kargil (2003) and Lakshya (2004) to Shershaah (2021) — the air force's role has remained largely in the background. The operational secrecy around Safed Sagar, combined with the technical complexity of depicting aerial combat, kept the story off screens for decades.

Tanya Bami, Netflix India's series head, called it "a first of its kind war drama series from India that will take the audience into the world of air force pilots." The streamer said the production uses world-class visual effects to recreate the high-altitude aerial sequences, including dogfights through narrow mountain passes.

A Crowded Patriotic Calendar

The August 7 premiere positions the series just ahead of Indian Independence Day on August 15, a window that has historically been prime territory for patriotic content on Indian streaming platforms. It also arrives as Netflix continues to invest heavily in Indian original content, following the success of titles like IC 814: The Kandahar Hijack.

For the diaspora, the series offers something that big-screen Kargil films often couldn't: a global platform and the intimacy of a multi-episode format to explore both the combat and the lives of the families left behind. The creators say they engaged directly with families connected to the real operation, weaving their experiences into the narrative alongside the aerial action sequences.

Operation Safed Sagar premieres on Netflix on August 7.
